# D4D Rubric20 - Twenty-Question Detailed Evaluation Rubric
# Schema Version: 2.1
# Last Updated: 2026-01-12

# =============================================================================
# FIELD REFERENCE GUIDE
# =============================================================================
# Use these exact field names when evaluating D4D files against the schema.
# The D4D schema uses a class-based structure, not dot-notation.
#
# Discovery & Access:
#   - id: Unique identifier (URI)
#   - doi: Digital Object Identifier
#   - rrid: Research Resource Identifier
#   - title: Dataset title
#   - description: Dataset description
#   - keywords: Search keywords (list)
#   - download_url: Download URL
#   - page: Landing page URL
#   - distribution_formats: DistributionFormat (list)
#
# Licensing & Governance:
#   - license_and_use_terms: LicenseAndUseTerms class
#   - ip_restrictions: IPRestrictions class
#   - regulatory_restrictions: ExportControlRegulatoryRestrictions class
#   - confidentiality_level: ConfidentialityLevelEnum
#
# Human Subjects:
#   - human_subject_research: HumanSubjectResearch class
#   - informed_consent: InformedConsent (list)
#   - participant_privacy: ParticipantPrivacy (list)
#   - participant_compensation: HumanSubjectCompensation class
#   - vulnerable_populations: VulnerablePopulations class
#   - ethical_reviews: EthicalReview (list)
#
# Data Composition:
#   - instances: Instance (list)
#   - variables: VariableMetadata (list)
#   - subpopulations: Subpopulation (list)
#   - is_tabular: Boolean
#   - is_deidentified: Deidentification class
#
# Data Quality:
#   - anomalies: DataAnomaly (list)
#   - known_biases: DatasetBias (list)
#   - known_limitations: DatasetLimitation (list)
#
# Use Guidance:
#   - intended_uses: IntendedUse (list)
#   - prohibited_uses: ProhibitedUse (list)
#   - discouraged_uses: DiscouragedUse (list)
#   - existing_uses: ExistingUse (list)
#
# Hierarchical Structure:
#   - resources: Dataset (list) - nested sub-resources
#   - parent_datasets: Dataset (list) - parent datasets
#   - related_datasets: DatasetRelationship (list) - typed relationships
#
# Funding & Motivation:
#   - purposes: Purpose (list)
#   - tasks: Task (list)
#   - funders: FundingMechanism (list)
#   - creators: Creator (list)
#
# Technical Methods:
#   - collection_mechanisms: CollectionMechanism (list)
#   - acquisition_methods: DataAcquisition (list)
#   - preprocessing_strategies: PreprocessingStrategy (list)
#   - cleaning_strategies: CleaningStrategy (list)
#   - labeling_strategies: LabelingStrategy (list)
#   - software_and_tools: Software (list)
#
# Versioning & Maintenance:
#   - version: Version string
#   - version_access: VersionAccess class
#   - updates: UpdatePlan class
#   - errata: Erratum (list)
#   - maintainers: Maintainer (list)
#   - was_derived_from: Source provenance
#   - release_notes: Release documentation
#
# Distribution:
#   - format: File format specification
#   - media_type: MIME type
#   - encoding: Character encoding
#   - bytes: File size in bytes
#   - conforms_to: Standards conformance
#   - conforms_to_schema: Schema conformance
#
# Other:
#   - publisher: Publishing organization
#   - citation: Recommended citation
#   - external_resources: ExternalResource (list)
#   - sensitive_elements: Sensitive content description
#   - content_warnings: Content warnings
#
# Data Protection & Compliance:
#   - data_protection_impacts: DataProtectionImpact (list)
#   - reidentification_risk: Re-identification risk assessment
#   - hipaa_compliant: ComplianceStatusEnum
#   - other_compliance: Other regulatory frameworks (list)
#   - governance_committee_contact: Governance committee contact person
#
# Responsible AI (CROISSANT RAI Alignment):
#   - future_use_impacts: FutureUseImpact (rai:dataSocialImpact) - Social impact analysis
#   - intended_uses: IntendedUse (rai:dataUseCases) - Explicit intended uses
#   - known_biases: DatasetBias (rai:dataBiases) - Categorized with BiasTypeEnum
#
# Data Quality & Documentation:
#   - missing_data_documentation: MissingDataDocumentation (list)
#   - annotation_analyses: AnnotationAnalysis (list)
#   - machine_annotation_tools: MachineAnnotationTool (list)
#   - raw_data_sources: RawDataSource (list)
#   - imputation_protocols: ImputationProtocol (list)
#
# Dataset Structure Flags:
#   - is_data_split: Boolean - Training/test split flag
#   - is_subpopulation: Boolean - Subpopulation subset flag
#   - confidential_elements: Confidentiality (list)
#
# Provenance (W3C PROV-O):
#   - was_derived_from: Source provenance with entity-activity-agent relationships
#   - Note: Provenance may be represented as text OR as W3C PROV-O graphs
#
# AI/ML Readiness (Bridge2AI):
#   - Reference: Bridge2AI AI-readiness characterization criteria
#   - Tool: Bridge2AI AI-readiness scorecard
#
# Data Sustainability:
#   - Persistent identifiers (DOI, ARK, Handle)
#   - Long-term governance plan
#   - Domain-appropriate repository
#   - Institutional commitment documentation
#
# Integration/Merging Capability:
#   - Common identifiers for cross-dataset integration
#   - Standardized formats for data harmonization
#   - Integration procedure documentation
# =============================================================================

d4d_evaluation_rubric:
  schema_version: "2.0"
  description: >
    A 20-question rubric for evaluating D4D YAML files for completeness, data quality,
    interoperability, and FAIR compliance. Each element is linked to specific metadata fields
    and tasks described in the D4D schema (data_sheets_schema_all.yaml).

    Total maximum score: 88 points (17 numeric questions × 5 points + 3 pass/fail questions × 1 point)

  scoring_scale:
    quantitative: 0–5
    qualitative: ["Pass", "Fail", "N/A"]

  rubric:
    # --------------------------- #
    # 1. Structural Completeness  #
    # --------------------------- #
    - id: 1
      name: "Field Completeness"
      description: >
        Proportion of mandatory schema fields populated including core identification,
        hierarchical structure, governance, and composition metadata.
      field: ["id", "title", "description", "keywords", "license_and_use_terms", "doi",
              "page", "creators", "purposes", "instances", "resources", "parent_datasets",
              "variables", "regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level"]
      method: "Count non-empty required fields; score by proportion filled."
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "≤40% fields populated"
        3: "≈70% fields populated"
        5: "≥90% fields populated"
      task_ref: [1, 2, 4, 6, 13]

    - id: 2
      name: "Entry Length Adequacy"
      description: "Checks whether narrative fields (e.g., description, purposes) have meaningful content length."
      field: ["description", "purposes"]
      method: "Measure average string length >200 characters."
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "<50 chars"
        3: "50–200 chars"
        5: ">200 chars"
      task_ref: [16, 17]

    - id: 3
      name: "Keyword Diversity"
      description: >
        Number of unique keywords provided to describe dataset topic coverage.

        Note: For datasets targeting multiple conditions (e.g., Bridge2AI-Voice with 50+ diseases),
        keywords may be supplemented by schema-defined condition lists. Check: (1) keywords field,
        (2) condition/disease fields in schema, (3) external ontology references (e.g., SNOMED CT,
        ICD codes).
      field: ["keywords"]
      method: "Count unique keywords."
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "<3 keywords"
        3: "3–7 keywords"
        5: "≥8 keywords"
      task_ref: [1, 2, 3]

    - id: 4
      name: "File Enumeration and Type Variety"
      description: >
        Number of distribution formats and file type diversity.

        Note: In Bridge2AI, multimodality is achieved by: (1) packaging separate single-modality
        datasets integrated on participant_id/sample_id, OR (2) single dataset with multiple data
        types. Check for: unified participant/sample identifiers across modalities. Multimodality
        is evaluated separately from AI/ML readiness (Q10).
      field: ["distribution_formats", "file_collections", "total_file_count"]
      method: "Count total formats and unique media types."
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "1 file type only"
        3: "2–3 file types"
        5: ">3 file types"
      task_ref: [94, 95]

    - id: 5
      name: "Data File Size Availability"
      description: "Presence of file size or dimensional metadata (bytes, instance counts, data splits)."
      field: ["total_size_bytes", "file_collections.total_bytes", "instances",
              "subsets.is_data_split", "splits", "subsets.is_subpopulation",
              "subpopulations"]
      method: "Detect numeric values for file size or instance counts."
      score_type: pass_fail
      scoring:
        Pass: "Numeric file size or dimension info found."
        Fail: "No file size/dimension metadata."
      task_ref: [69, 70]

    # --------------------------- #
    # 2. Metadata Quality & Content #
    # --------------------------- #
    - id: 6
      name: "Dataset Identification Metadata"
      description: >
        Presence of unique identifiers such as DOI, RRID, or persistent URLs, AND hosting
        platform identification (publisher or repository).

        Note: Dataset identification should include both persistent identifiers AND hosting
        platform information (e.g., PhysioNet, Dataverse, Zenodo, institutional repositories).
      field: ["doi", "id", "page", "publisher"]
      method: "Check for non-null DOI or equivalent identifier AND publisher/platform."
      score_type: pass_fail
      scoring:
        Pass: "At least one persistent ID found."
        Fail: "No persistent ID or link."
      task_ref: [2, 7]

    - id: 7
      name: "Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness"
      description: "Checks presence of funding sources, grants, institutional sponsors, and creator affiliations."
      field: ["funders", "creators"]
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "No funding data"
        3: "Funding agency or creator info but missing grants/affiliations"
        5: "Funders with grants + creators with affiliations"
      task_ref: [22, 23, 24, 25]

    - id: 8
      name: "Ethical and Privacy Declarations"
      description: >
        Comprehensive ethics coverage including IRB approval, deidentification, privacy protections,
        informed consent, participant compensation, vulnerable population safeguards, data protection
        impact assessments (DPIA), and re-identification risk analysis.

        Note: Sensitive data includes protected health information (PHI) such as: voice recordings,
        physical activity data (step counts), retinal images, genetic data, location data, biometric
        identifiers, and other individually identifiable health information requiring special protections.
      field: ["ethical_reviews", "human_subject_research", "is_deidentified",
              "participant_privacy", "participant_compensation", "at_risk_populations",
              "informed_consent", "data_protection_impacts",
              "participant_privacy.reidentification_risk"]
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "No ethics fields present"
        3: "Basic ethics (IRB + deidentification)"
        5: "Comprehensive (ethics + DPIA + re-identification risk + all human subjects protections)"
      task_ref: [59, 76, 80, 84]
      applies_to: ["Bridge2AI-Voice", "AI-READI"]

    - id: 9
      name: "Access Requirements and Governance Documentation"
      description: >
        Determines if access policy, license, IP restrictions, regulatory restrictions,
        confidentiality level, multi-jurisdiction compliance, and governance contacts are clearly defined.

        Note: In Bridge2AI, license types include: (1) CM4AI uses CC-BY-NC-SA (permissive license),
        (2) AI-READi, CHORUS, VOICE use Data Use Agreements (controlled access). Avoid misleading
        terms like "Open" or "Public" - instead use: permissive license (e.g., CC-BY, CC-BY-NC-SA)
        or openly accessible with DUA (requires signed agreement). Access tiers: (1) No authentication,
        (2) Registration required, (3) DUA required, (4) IRB/committee approval required.
      field: ["license_and_use_terms", "ip_restrictions", "regulatory_restrictions",
              "regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level",
              "regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant",
              "regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance",
              "regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact"]
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "No license or access info"
        3: "License + basic restrictions"
        5: "License + multi-jurisdiction compliance + confidentiality classification + governance contact"
      task_ref: [11, 12, 87, 88]
      applies_to: ["Bridge2AI-Voice", "Dataverse"]

    - id: 10
      name: "Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration"
      description: >
        Presence of standard formats, ontologies, schema conformance (e.g., Parquet, TSV, LinkML),
        cross-platform dataset linkages with typed relationships, AND dataset integration capability.

        Note: Evaluation aligned with Bridge2AI AI/ML readiness characterization criteria (FAIRness,
        semantic/statistical characterization, governance, quality, pre-model XAI, ethics, computability).
        Reference: https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.12.18.629172v1 and Bridge2AI AI-readiness
        scorecard tool.

        All Bridge2AI datasets are designed for AI/ML use. This question evaluates HOW WELL the dataset
        supports AI/ML (interoperability, standardization), not WHETHER it supports AI/ML.

        Dataset integration capability: Check for common identifiers for cross-dataset linking,
        standardized formats for data harmonization, and documented integration procedures.
      field: ["distribution_formats", "conforms_to_schema", "file_collections.compression",
              "conforms_to", "external_resources", "related_datasets"]
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "Non-standard or unspecified format"
        3: "Standard format but no schema reference"
        5: "Standard formats + schema/ontology compliance + integration capability"
      task_ref: [50, 67, 96, 97]
      applies_to: ["Bridge2AI-Voice", "Health Nexus"]

    # --------------------------- #
    # 3. Technical Documentation  #
    # --------------------------- #
    - id: 11
      name: "Tool and Software Transparency"
      description: >
        Mentions of preprocessing, cleaning, and labeling strategies with software tools
        used in data preparation, including annotation quality metrics and imputation protocols.

        Note: Preprocessing and collection metadata may be represented as structured text descriptions
        OR as machine-readable provenance graphs (e.g., W3C PROV-O, workflow graphs). Evaluation should
        check for: (1) structured text descriptions OR (2) graph representations with entity-activity-agent
        relationships. Both formats are acceptable. Some datasets (e.g., CM4AI) describe preprocessing in
        provenance graphs rather than text.
      field: ["preprocessing_strategies", "cleaning_strategies", "labeling_strategies",
              "machine_annotation_tools", "annotation_analyses", "imputation_protocols"]
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "No software tools documented"
        3: "At least one strategy or tool listed"
        5: "Comprehensive strategies with software versions/URLs, annotation quality, and imputation protocols"
      task_ref: [64, 65, 66]
      applies_to: ["Bridge2AI-Voice"]

    - id: 12
      name: "Collection Protocol Clarity"
      description: >
        Evaluates description completeness of data collection mechanisms, acquisition methods,
        data collectors, collection timeframes, and raw data sources.
      field: ["acquisition_methods", "collection_mechanisms", "data_collectors",
              "collection_timeframes", "raw_data_sources"]
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "No collection description"
        3: "Partial description (e.g., mechanism only)"
        5: "Full collection protocol with methods, collectors, and timeframes"
      task_ref: [46, 47, 48, 49]
      applies_to: ["Bridge2AI-Voice", "AI-READI"]

    - id: 13
      name: "Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability"
      description: >
        Presence of version information, version access methods, errata, update plans, release notes
        with dates, AND data sustainability indicators (persistent identifiers, long-term governance
        plan, domain-appropriate repository, institutional commitment documentation).

        Note: Data sustainability evaluation checks for: (1) persistent identifiers (DOI, ARK, Handle),
        (2) long-term governance plan, (3) domain-appropriate repository (e.g., PhysioNet for biomedical
        data), (4) institutional commitment or preservation funding. Sustainable datasets have clear
        maintenance plans beyond initial publication.
      field: ["version", "version_access", "errata", "updates", "maintainers", "doi",
              "publisher"]
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "Single version only, no sustainability plan"
        3: "Version number + basic access info + persistent ID"
        5: "Comprehensive versioning + full sustainability documentation (governance + repository + commitment)"
      task_ref: [8, 95]
      applies_to: ["Bridge2AI-Voice", "Dataverse"]

    - id: 14
      name: "Associated Publications"
      description: >
        Presence of formal citations or DOI-linked references.

        Note: All Bridge2AI datasets require citation metadata if reused. Evaluation checks for:
        (1) formatted citation string (DataCite or BibTeX format), (2) DOI, (3) citation instructions
        in documentation. Datasets without citation metadata receive 0 points, as citation is mandatory
        for proper attribution and reproducibility in Bridge2AI.
      field: ["citation", "external_resources", "doi"]
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "No publications cited (citation metadata missing - MANDATORY for Bridge2AI)"
        3: "One citation or reference with DOI"
        5: "Multiple references with DOI cross-links + formatted citation + citation instructions"
      task_ref: [9, 30]
      applies_to: ["Bridge2AI-Voice", "AI-READI"]

    - id: 15
      name: "Human Subject Representation"
      description: >
        Indicates inclusion of human subjects with demographic diversity, subpopulation details,
        vulnerable population protections, and missing data documentation.
      field: ["subpopulations", "instances", "at_risk_populations",
              "subsets.is_subpopulation", "missing_data_documentation"]
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "No human subject information"
        3: "General human data without subgroup description"
        5: "Detailed demographics, subpopulations, and inclusion/exclusion criteria"
      task_ref: [31, 35, 37]
      applies_to: ["Bridge2AI-Voice", "AI-READI"]

    # --------------------------- #
    # 4. FAIRness & Accessibility #
    # --------------------------- #
    - id: 16
      name: "Findability (Persistent Links)"
      description: "Dataset includes persistent URLs, DOI, and identifier for access and documentation."
      field: ["page", "doi", "id"]
      score_type: pass_fail
      scoring:
        Pass: "At least one persistent identifier present."
        Fail: "No persistent identifiers found."
      task_ref: [7, 14, 91]

    - id: 17
      name: "Accessibility (Access Mechanism)"
      description: >
        Describes how users can obtain the dataset (download URL, distribution formats, access policy).

        Note: "Public" does not mean "no restrictions." Even openly accessible datasets may require
        signed Data Use Agreements (DUAs). Distinguish between access tiers: (1) No authentication
        required (truly public), (2) Registration required (email/account), (3) DUA required (signed
        agreement), (4) IRB/committee approval required (restricted access). For example, AI-READi is
        openly accessible but requires a DUA - it is NOT "public" in the unrestricted sense.
      field: ["download_url", "distribution_formats", "license_and_use_terms"]
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "Unclear access method"
        3: "Partially described access mechanism (access tier unclear)"
        5: "Fully defined access path with explicit access tier (download URL, formats, policy, access requirements)"
      task_ref: [11, 87, 90]
      applies_to: ["Dataverse", "PhysioNet"]

    - id: 18
      name: "Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact"
      description: >
        License is clearly defined with explicit use guidance including intended uses,
        prohibited uses, discouraged uses, AND comprehensive social impact analysis with risk
        identification and mitigation strategies (CROISSANT RAI aligned).
      field: ["license_and_use_terms", "intended_uses", "prohibited_uses",
              "discouraged_uses", "future_use_impacts"]
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "No license or use guidance"
        3: "License + basic use guidance"
        5: "License + comprehensive use guidance + social impact analysis with mitigation strategies"
      task_ref: [13, 88]

    - id: 19
      name: "Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality"
      description: >
        Presence of version access, errata, update plans, source derivation, parent dataset linkages,
        missing data documentation, data split indicators, AND provenance graph representation.

        Note: Provenance is a transparent graph of origins and processing of data (W3C PROV-O standard:
        https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/), NOT just version changes. Evaluation checks for:
        (1) Entity-activity-agent relationships, (2) Processing lineage, (3) Derivation paths.

        Scoring distinction:
        - Version history alone (version numbers, errata, updates) = 3 points
        - Full provenance graph (W3C PROV-O with entity-activity-agent relationships, processing
          lineage, derivation paths) = 5 points

        Provenance may be represented as text OR as W3C PROV-O graphs. Both formats are acceptable
        if they provide complete lineage information.
      field: ["version_access", "errata", "updates", "was_derived_from", "parent_datasets",
              "missing_data_documentation", "subsets.is_data_split", "splits",
              "raw_data_sources"]
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "No provenance metadata"
        3: "Version history (version numbers, errata, updates) but no full provenance graph"
        5: "Full provenance graph with entity-activity-agent relationships, processing lineage, and derivation paths"
      task_ref: [3, 8, 95]

    - id: 20
      name: "Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment"
      description: >
        Metadata documents known biases using standardized taxonomies (BiasTypeEnum, AIO)
        aligned with CROISSANT RAI standards, and includes fairness analysis. Assesses whether
        biases are categorized systematically (e.g., selection_bias, measurement_bias,
        algorithmic_bias, ecological_fallacy) with mappings to AI Ontology (AIO).
      field: ["known_biases", "future_use_impacts"]
      score_type: numeric
      scoring:
        0: "No bias documentation"
        3: "Basic bias identification without taxonomy"
        5: "Comprehensive bias categorization using standard taxonomy (AIO/CROISSANT RAI) + fairness analysis"
      task_ref: [varies]
      applies_to: ["Bridge2AI-Voice", "AI-READI", "CM4AI", "CHORUS"]

96	purposes:
97	- response: >-
98	    To create a flagship, standardized and ethically sourced dataset of 10,000 voices linked to
99	    health information, to fuel research and discovery in voice biomarkers and to promote the
100	    integration of voice as a biomarker of health in clinical care. The multi-site IRB protocol
101	    for the underlying data acquisition study states a sample size of 30,000 participants, to be
102	    reached through collaboration with other participating institutions and existing cohorts.
103	  source_caveats: >-
104	    The project documentation states a target of 10,000 voices and an anticipated enrollment of
105	    10,000 by 2027, while the multi-site IRB protocol, a source of the same rank, states a sample
106	    size of 30,000 participants; the JAMA Otolaryngology viewpoint, a lower-ranked source, also
107	    states 30,000 human voices. The equal-ranked sources disagree, so both figures are recorded in
108	    the response above.
109	- response: >-
110	    To enable the development, benchmarking and validation of clinically applicable
111	    machine-learning models that diagnose a wide range of health conditions from voice, including
112	    vocal pathologies and neurological, psychiatric, respiratory and pediatric voice disorders.
113	- response: >-
114	    To introduce the field of acoustic biomarkers by developing new standards for acoustic and
115	    voice data collection, analysis and interoperability for voice AI research, including new
116	    bioinformatics standards for voice data and benchmarks of diversity metrics that minimize the
117	    risk of algorithmic bias.
118	- response: >-
119	    To develop and disseminate ethical, legal and governance norms for voice data, addressing
120	    voice re-identification risk, voice AI hacking, consent to voice data collection and sharing,
121	    and the influence of gender and racial diversity on voice AI.

123	addressing_gaps:
124	- response: >-
125	    Previous studies of machine-learning-based voice diagnosis produced promising results, but
126	    their sample sizes were too small or they lacked the key metadata needed for training robust,
127	    clinically useful models; the dataset supplies a large, diverse and well-documented resource
128	    in their place.
129	- response: >-
130	    Comparing studies and pooling data has been difficult because there are no established
131	    standards for how voice and other acoustic data are measured and collected; the consortium
132	    developed and published standardized multi-disorder acquisition protocols alongside the data.
133	- response: >-
134	    Industry holds vast amounts of voice data but lacks accurate clinical and demographic
135	    information, and its datasets are private, which prevents external auditing of training data
136	    and of fair representation of diverse populations; this dataset is openly documented and
137	    linked to clinically validated diagnoses.
138	- response: >-
139	    Existing open-source voice datasets are limited in size, quality and diversity, and voice data
140	    have rarely been linked to multimodal health biomarkers; this dataset links acoustic data to
141	    demographics, confounders, validated questionnaires and clinician-confirmed diagnoses.

351	  identifiable_elements_present: false
352	  method: >-
353	    HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification, removal of selected indirect identifiers and highly
354	    sensitive non-identifying elements, and withholding of all raw audio.
355	  identifiers_removed: >-
356	    Names, civic addresses and social security numbers; geographic locators, including state and
357	    province, with only country of collection retained; date information at any resolution finer
358	    than years; phone and fax numbers, email addresses, IP addresses, medical record numbers,
359	    health plan beneficiary numbers, device identifiers, license numbers, account numbers, vehicle
360	    identifiers, website URLs, full-face photographs, biometric identifiers and other unique
361	    identifiers; narrative free-text fields and transcripts of free speech; selected demographic
362	    identifiers and information about household composition or cultural identity; and all raw
363	    voice recordings.
364	  deidentification_details: >-
365	    Direct identifiers were removed; indirect identifiers were removed where they created a
366	    significant risk of re-identification through combination with public data. Dates were rebased
367	    or replaced by integers, geographic information was generalized, and narrative text fields were
368	    removed. Spectrograms, mel spectrograms, MFCCs, phonetic posteriorgrams and articulatory
369	    estimates were excluded where the audio contained free speech, and features for sensitive
370	    records and audio checks were removed; static features that do not encode sensitive content
371	    were retained. Raw audio transcripts were reviewed and recordings containing potentially
372	    identifying information or external voices were removed from the release. K-anonymization with
373	    k greater than or equal to two is not achieved, and voice itself can never be fully
374	    de-identified, which is why the waveforms are released only under controlled access.

454	raw_data_sources:
455	- source_description: >-
456	    Raw voice, speech, breathing and cough audio recordings captured by the Bridge2AI-Voice
457	    application, together with the questionnaire and clinical responses recorded alongside them.
458	  source_type: Prospectively collected audio recordings and questionnaire responses
459	  raw_data_format: >-
460	    WAV audio, converted to monaural and resampled to 16 kHz before feature extraction; REDCap and
461	    ReproSchema exports converted to tab-delimited phenotype tables.
462	  access_details: >-
463	    Raw audio is not included in the PhysioNet release. Access requires a completed Data Access
464	    Request Form and Data Use Agreement, review by the Data Access Compliance Office
465	    (DACO@b2ai-voice.org) and a signed Data Transfer and Use Agreement from an authorized
466	    institutional official; approved users receive the adult cohort audio through Synapse at
467	    https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/. The de-identified raw data are retained but are
468	    not publicly accessible.

470	preprocessing_strategies:
471	- preprocessing_details: >-
472	    Raw audio was converted to monaural and resampled to 16 kHz with a Butterworth anti-aliasing
473	    filter applied.
474	- preprocessing_details: >-
475	    Spectrograms of dimension 201 by T were computed with a short-time fast Fourier transform
476	    using a 25 ms window, a 10 ms hop and a 400-point FFT, then downsampled by a factor of two in
477	    the time domain.
478	- preprocessing_details: >-
479	    Mel spectrograms with 60 mel bins and 60 mel-frequency cepstral coefficients were computed
480	    with the same window, hop and FFT settings.
481	- preprocessing_details: >-
482	    Articulatory features were produced with the Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc) package at
483	    50 Hz, giving electromagnetic articulography traces for six articulators (tongue dorsum,
484	    tongue body, tongue tip, lower incisor, upper lip and lower lip) together with loudness,
485	    periodicity and pitch estimates.
486	- preprocessing_details: >-
487	    Phonetic posteriorgrams over 40 phoneme categories were generated at 100 Hz with the ppgs
488	    package.
489	- preprocessing_details: >-
490	    Static acoustic, phonetic and prosodic features were extracted with openSMILE, Praat and
491	    parselmouth, and pitch contours with torchaudio, producing one row per recording in
492	    static_features.tsv.
493	- preprocessing_details: >-
494	    Raw audio files and questionnaire data retrieved from ReproSchema-UI or exported from REDCap
495	    were converted to a structure compliant with the Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0, with
496	    phenotype tables grouped into confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaire
497	    and task folders.
498	- preprocessing_details: >-
499	    All processing was performed with the open-source b2aiprep library, which organizes and
500	    preprocesses the dataset, and senselab, which processes the audio files; version 3.1.0 was
501	    generated with b2aiprep v3.0.0.
502	
503	cleaning_strategies:
504	- cleaning_details: >-
505	    No data cleaning was performed. An audit protocol was applied instead: missingness tables were
506	    generated, distributions and outliers checked, categorical responses checked against the
507	    schema, and quality control metrics run on the audio, including the amount of silence, the
508	    duration, and for speech tasks the agreement of the produced speech with the intended passage.
509	    From version 3.1.0 the resulting audio quality metrics are released alongside the features.
510	
511	labeling_strategies:
512	- labeling_details: >-
513	    Diagnostic labels are the result of a clinical assessment of the participant. At each site a
514	    local clinician provided the diagnosis based on a clinical interview and appropriate work-up,
515	    using the gold-standard validation methods defined per cohort, such as laryngoscopy images and
516	    stroboscopy videos for voice disorders, CT and MRI of the brain for neurological disorders,
517	    and spirometry with flow-volume loops for airway conditions.

519	  data_annotation_protocol: Bridge2AI-Voice protocols and ICD-10 codes.
520	  annotator_demographics:
521	  - >-
522	    Typically the clinician at the site of data collection, or a clinician external to the study
523	    who had made a prior diagnostic assessment; a single labeler per instance.
524	- labeling_details: >-
525	    For the psychiatric disorders cohort the assessment was determined from the participant's
526	    electronic health record or from an active prescription, recorded outside the data collection
527	    session by an appropriately licensed clinician.

536	    dataset is intended to address is reported to vary widely. Certain machine-generated

575	  derivation: >-
576	    Short-time fast Fourier transform of the 16 kHz monaural waveform with a 25 ms window, a 10 ms
577	    hop and a 400-point FFT, downsampled by a factor of two in the time domain; dimension 201 by T.
578	  measurement_technique: torchaudio
579	  quality_notes: >-
580	    Absent for recordings that contain free speech, for sensitive records and for audio checks,
581	    and for recordings whose length or other properties prevented generation.
582	- variable_name: mel_spectrogram
583	  data_type: array
584	  derivation: >-
585	    Mel spectrogram with 60 mel bins computed with a 25 ms window, a 10 ms hop and a 400-point
586	    FFT; dimension 60 by T.
587	  measurement_technique: torchaudio
588	- variable_name: mfcc
589	  data_type: array
590	  derivation: >-
591	    Sixty mel-frequency cepstral coefficients computed from the mel spectrograms with the same
592	    window, hop and FFT parameters; dimension 60 by T.
593	  measurement_technique: torchaudio
594	- variable_name: pitch
595	  data_type: array
596	  derivation: >-
597	    Detected pitch (fundamental frequency) over time, of dimension T, with a minimum pitch of 80
598	    and a maximum of 500.
599	  measurement_technique: torchaudio
600	  minimum_value: 80.0
601	  maximum_value: 500.0
602	- variable_name: sparc_ema
603	  data_type: array
604	  derivation: >-
605	    Estimated electromagnetic articulography produced by a deep learning model at 50 Hz, of
606	    dimension T by 12, the twelve channels being the X and Y positions of six articulators: tongue
607	    dorsum, tongue body, tongue tip, lower incisor, upper lip and lower lip.
608	  measurement_technique: Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc)
609	- variable_name: sparc_loudness
610	  data_type: array
611	  derivation: >-
612	    Estimated loudness based on the average absolute amplitude of the audio waveform, of dimension
613	    T, computed with 20 ms windows.
614	  measurement_technique: Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc)
615	- variable_name: sparc_periodicity
616	  data_type: array
617	  derivation: >-
618	    Estimated periodicity, the confidence of pitch presence, derived from the audio with 20 ms
619	    windows, of dimension T.
620	  measurement_technique: Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc)
621	- variable_name: sparc_pitch
622	  data_type: array
623	  derivation: >-
624	    Estimated fundamental frequency of the audio signal computed with a different algorithm from
625	    the torchaudio pitch, over a range of 50 to 550 Hz, of dimension T.
626	  measurement_technique: Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc)
627	  unit: Hz
628	  minimum_value: 50.0
629	  maximum_value: 550.0
630	- variable_name: ppgs
631	  data_type: array
632	  derivation: >-
633	    Phonetic posteriorgram probabilities across 40 phoneme categories at a frame rate of 100 Hz,
634	    of dimension 40 by T.
635	  measurement_technique: ppgs package
636	  quality_notes: >-
637	    Removed for sensitive records and audio checks, and absent where the audio contained free
638	    speech.

id: doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66
name: Bridge2AI-Voice
title: "Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information"
description: >-
  Bridge2AI-Voice is an ethically sourced, demographically diverse dataset of voice, speech,
  breathing and cough recordings linked to health information, generated by the Bridge2AI-Voice
  consortium under the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program. Version 3.1.0 covers 833 adult
  participants recruited at five sites in North America and selected for conditions that manifest
  in the voice waveform: voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and
  psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders, and controls. Participants completed a standardized
  protocol of acoustic tasks on a tablet application together with demographic questions,
  confounder questions, disease-specific clinical forms and validated questionnaires, and consented
  to clinician review of their records for gold-standard validation of diagnoses. The published
  release contains only data considered low risk: dense per-recording features derived from the
  waveforms (spectrograms, mel spectrograms, mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, pitch contours,
  Speech Articulatory Coding articulatory traces with loudness, periodicity and pitch, and phonetic
  posteriorgrams) distributed as Parquet, together with static openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth and
  torchaudio features, audio quality metrics, per-recording metadata, and phenotype tables covering
  enrollment, demographics, confounders, diagnoses, questionnaires and task metadata, each
  accompanied by a JSON data dictionary. The original voice recordings are withheld from this
  release and distributed only under controlled access.
version: "3.1.0"
status: published
issued: '2026-05-01T00:00:00Z'

  Raw voice, speech, breathing and cough audio recordings captured with the Bridge2AI-Voice
  application, together with questionnaire and clinical data exported from REDCap.
conforms_to: >-
  Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS) v1.9.0, applied to the audio dataset layout and the
  phenotype folder organization rather than to the Parquet feature files of the published
  feature-only release.

citation: >-
  Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., Elemento, O., Powell, M., Dorr, D., Payne, P.,
  Ravitsky, V., Belisle-Pipon, J., Bahr, R., Watts, S., Bolser, D., Siu, J., Lerner-Ellis, J.,
  Rudzicz, F., Boyer, M., Abdel-Aty, Y., Ahmed Syed, T., Anibal, J., ... Ghosh, S. (2026).
  Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information
  (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66
notes: >-
  The adult protocol records 22 acoustic tasks through the application, grouped as non-voice/
  non-speech (respiration, voluntary cough, breath sounds), voice/non-speech (prolonged vowel,
  maximum phonation time, glides, loudness, diadochokinesis) and speech (Rainbow Passage,
  Caterpillar Passage, CAPE-V sentences, free speech, picture description, story recall, animal
  fluency, open response questions, word-color Stroop, productive vocabulary, random item
  generation, Cinderella story), with cohort-specific tasks assigned by disease category.
source_caveats: >-
  The referent of this record is the adult Bridge2AI-Voice feature-only release published on
  PhysioNet, and `id` carries the version-specific DOI for v3.1.0; the version-independent
  concept DOI 10.13026/37yb-1t42 is recorded separately in `version_access.latest_version_doi`
  and in a `related_datasets` entry. Counts and release facts are taken from the PhysioNet
  v3.1.0 record, the highest-ranked non-superseded source. The project documentation describes
  version 3.0 as containing about 61,937 voice-derived recordings from 833 adult participants,
  whereas the PhysioNet releases report per-feature record counts (29,278 spectrogram, mel
  spectrogram and MFCC records and 32,522 pitch records in v3.1.0) rather than a single recording
  total; the PhysioNet figures are used here. The project documentation also describes
  distribution through the Health Data Nexus, which hosted version 1.0; versions 1.1 onward are
  published on PhysioNet, and the PhysioNet statement is preferred. The PhysioNet v3.1.0 release
  names 120 authors; the creators recorded here are the co-principal investigators and lead
  investigators identified in the project documentation. The variables listed in `variables` are
  the identifying and dense-feature columns shared across the released files, not a complete
  enumeration of the released columns, which run to the whole of the phenotype tables and every
  static feature described in the accompanying data dictionaries. The healthsheet states that the
  dataset is self-contained; the external resources recorded here are supporting code, data
  dictionaries and the controlled-access route for raw audio rather than dependencies of the
  released files.

purposes:
- response: >-
    To create a flagship, standardized and ethically sourced dataset of 10,000 voices linked to
    health information, to fuel research and discovery in voice biomarkers and to promote the
    integration of voice as a biomarker of health in clinical care. The multi-site IRB protocol
    for the underlying data acquisition study states a sample size of 30,000 participants, to be
    reached through collaboration with other participating institutions and existing cohorts.
  source_caveats: >-
    The project documentation states a target of 10,000 voices and an anticipated enrollment of
    10,000 by 2027, while the multi-site IRB protocol, a source of the same rank, states a sample
    size of 30,000 participants; the JAMA Otolaryngology viewpoint, a lower-ranked source, also
    states 30,000 human voices. The equal-ranked sources disagree, so both figures are recorded in
    the response above.
- response: >-
    To enable the development, benchmarking and validation of clinically applicable
    machine-learning models that diagnose a wide range of health conditions from voice, including
    vocal pathologies and neurological, psychiatric, respiratory and pediatric voice disorders.
- response: >-
    To introduce the field of acoustic biomarkers by developing new standards for acoustic and
    voice data collection, analysis and interoperability for voice AI research, including new
    bioinformatics standards for voice data and benchmarks of diversity metrics that minimize the
    risk of algorithmic bias.
- response: >-
    To develop and disseminate ethical, legal and governance norms for voice data, addressing
    voice re-identification risk, voice AI hacking, consent to voice data collection and sharing,
    and the influence of gender and racial diversity on voice AI.

addressing_gaps:
- response: >-
    Previous studies of machine-learning-based voice diagnosis produced promising results, but
    their sample sizes were too small or they lacked the key metadata needed for training robust,
    clinically useful models; the dataset supplies a large, diverse and well-documented resource
    in their place.
- response: >-
    Comparing studies and pooling data has been difficult because there are no established
    standards for how voice and other acoustic data are measured and collected; the consortium
    developed and published standardized multi-disorder acquisition protocols alongside the data.
- response: >-
    Industry holds vast amounts of voice data but lacks accurate clinical and demographic
    information, and its datasets are private, which prevents external auditing of training data
    and of fair representation of diverse populations; this dataset is openly documented and
    linked to clinically validated diagnoses.
- response: >-
    Existing open-source voice datasets are limited in size, quality and diversity, and voice data
    have rarely been linked to multimodal health biomarkers; this dataset links acoustic data to
    demographics, confounders, validated questionnaires and clinician-confirmed diagnoses.

tasks:
- response: >-
    Detection and classification of disease from voice, using diagnostic labels spanning vocal
    pathologies, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, psychiatric conditions and
    respiratory disorders.
- response: >-
    Pretraining, fine-tuning, benchmarking and validation of artificial intelligence and machine
    learning models on voice, speech and respiratory audio features.

instances:
- instance_type: Study participant
  counts: 833
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:4
  label: true
  label_description: >-
    Each participant carries a diagnostic label corresponding to one of the disease cohorts
    (voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric
    disorders, respiratory disorders) or to the control group, assigned by a clinician at the site
    of data collection.
  notes: >-
    Each instance represents a person. A participant may have more than one recording session, so
    phenotype and feature files may contain more than one row per participant, and responses need
    not agree across sessions. Participant-level information is distributed as tab-separated
    phenotype tables.
- instance_type: Derived feature record for a single audio recording
  data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30
  data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:36
  label: false
  notes: >-
    Record counts differ by feature type in version 3.1.0: 29,278 records each for spectrograms,
    mel spectrograms and mel-frequency cepstral coefficients; 32,522 torchaudio pitch records;
    28,640 sparc electromagnetic articulography records; 31,855 sparc loudness records; 31,872
    sparc periodicity and sparc pitch records; and 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram records. Some
    recordings could not yield certain features because of length or other issues and are absent
    from those files.

subpopulations:
- subpopulation_elements_present: true
  identification: >-
    Disease cohort categories assigned at enrollment from a clinical diagnosis: voice disorders,
    neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory
    disorders, pediatric voice and speech disorders, and controls.
  distribution: >-
    The public releases do not contain an equal distribution of these disease categories, and the
    adult release contains no pediatric participants; the pediatric cohort is published as a
    separate dataset.
- subpopulation_elements_present: true
  identification: >-
    Demographic sub-populations recorded in the demographics phenotype table: age, gender, sex,
    ethnicity and socioeconomic status.
  distribution: >-
    The dataset is skewed by site and by demographic factors; users are advised to consider the
    multivariate distribution when assessing utility for a given question.

relationships:
- relationship_details: >-
    Relationships between individual instances are not made explicit; participants are unrelated
    to one another. Feature records are linked to their participant and recording session through
    the participant_id and session_id fields, and a participant may have several sessions.

splits:
- split_details: >-
    No recommended train, validation or test splits are provided. Researchers are encouraged to
    create their own splits according to their requirements, taking account of the skews in
    disorder category, site and demographics.

anomalies:
- anomaly_details: >-
    Different sites used different collection configurations, and the collection protocol changed
    over the course of the study.
- anomaly_details: >-
    Noise artifacts are present in the recordings; the head-mounted headset microphone could sit
    at slightly different distances from participant to participant.
- anomaly_details: >-
    Diagnostic practices vary between sites and clinicians, and questionnaire responses may be
    inaccurate or under-reported.
- anomaly_details: >-
    Some recordings could not produce particular features because of recording length or other
    issues and are therefore missing from the corresponding feature files, so record counts differ
    between feature types.
- anomaly_details: >-
    Some Parquet files distributed in version 3.0.0 were broken and were fixed in version 3.1.0.

missing_data_documentation:
- missing_data_patterns: >-
    Phenotype files contain a row for a participant only where at least one column is non-missing.
    Each participant answered a common set of questions and then additional questions relevant to
    their primary diagnostic category, so disease-specific instruments are absent for participants
    outside that cohort. Record counts also differ across the dense feature files.
  missing_data_causes: >-
    Some questions are optional; data collection irregularities caused information to be missing
    from individual instances; some recordings could not yield particular features; and dense
    features derived from free-speech audio, along with sensitive records and audio checks, were
    removed during de-identification.
  handling_strategy: >-
    No imputation is performed. A missingness table is included with the dataset, and generating
    missingness tables is the first step of the audit protocol applied before each release.

content_warnings:
- content_warnings_present: true
  warnings:
  - >-
    The collection includes free speech tasks whose transcription may contain offensive or
    distressing content, since participants are responsible for their choice of language; the
    documentation states that while such content is unlikely it cannot be completely avoided.
    Dense features and transcripts derived from free-speech prompts were removed from the released
    feature set, and audio recordings containing potentially identifying information or external
    voices were removed. Questionnaire content covers depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress
    and other psychiatric symptoms.

confidential_elements:
- confidential_elements_present: false
  confidentiality_details: >-
    The healthsheet reports that the released dataset contains no data protected by legal
    privilege or doctor-patient confidentiality. Raw voice recordings, which carry re-identification
    risk, are withheld from this release and distributed only under controlled access.

sensitive_elements:
- sensitive_elements_present: true
  sensitivity_details: The dataset includes race and ethnic origin information.
- sensitive_elements_present: true
  sensitivity_details: The dataset includes sexual orientation information.
- sensitive_elements_present: true
  sensitivity_details: >-
    The dataset includes socioeconomic and health information, including clinical diagnoses and
    validated psychiatric and respiratory questionnaire responses.
  notes: >-
    Fields encoded as sensitive in the REDCap data dictionary were removed before release, as were
    non-identifying elements revealing highly sensitive information such as household income,
    mental health status and traumatic life experiences.

is_deidentified:
  identifiable_elements_present: false
  method: >-
    HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification, removal of selected indirect identifiers and highly
    sensitive non-identifying elements, and withholding of all raw audio.
  identifiers_removed: >-
    Names, civic addresses and social security numbers; geographic locators, including state and
    province, with only country of collection retained; date information at any resolution finer
    than years; phone and fax numbers, email addresses, IP addresses, medical record numbers,
    health plan beneficiary numbers, device identifiers, license numbers, account numbers, vehicle
    identifiers, website URLs, full-face photographs, biometric identifiers and other unique
    identifiers; narrative free-text fields and transcripts of free speech; selected demographic
    identifiers and information about household composition or cultural identity; and all raw
    voice recordings.
  deidentification_details: >-
    Direct identifiers were removed; indirect identifiers were removed where they created a
    significant risk of re-identification through combination with public data. Dates were rebased
    or replaced by integers, geographic information was generalized, and narrative text fields were
    removed. Spectrograms, mel spectrograms, MFCCs, phonetic posteriorgrams and articulatory
    estimates were excluded where the audio contained free speech, and features for sensitive
    records and audio checks were removed; static features that do not encode sensitive content
    were retained. Raw audio transcripts were reviewed and recordings containing potentially
    identifying information or external voices were removed from the release. K-anonymization with
    k greater than or equal to two is not achieved, and voice itself can never be fully
    de-identified, which is why the waveforms are released only under controlled access.

acquisition_methods:
- was_directly_observed: true
  was_reported_by_subjects: true
  acquisition_details: >-
    Acoustic tasks were recorded directly from participants with a tablet application, while
    demographics, confounders and validated questionnaires were self-reported by participants.
- was_validated_verified: true
  acquisition_details: >-
    Clinical diagnoses were verified by clinicians reviewing audio and imaging data, electronic
    health records, or medication prescriptions, against cohort-specific gold standards such as
    laryngoscopy and stroboscopy, CT and MRI of the brain, and spirometry with flow-volume loops.
- was_inferred_derived: true
  acquisition_details: >-
    All released feature data were derived computationally from the raw waveforms with open-source
    toolkits, and transcriptions were generated with an automatic speech recognition model.

collection_mechanisms:
- mechanism_details: >-
    A custom Bridge2AI-Voice application running on a tablet collected acoustic tasks, surveys and
    validated questionnaires, and sent data over a secure HTTPS protocol to HIPAA-compliant cloud
    storage provided by NIH STRIDES partners.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Recordings were made on iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) with an
    Avid AE-36 head-mounted microphone connected through an Apple dongle; distinct iPad devices
    were used at each site.
- mechanism_details: >-
    Instruments, the data dictionary and metadata are maintained in REDCap and published openly;
    data were exported and converted from REDCap with the consortium's open-source library.

collection_timeframes:
- timeframe_details: >-
    The healthsheet states that the data were collected over a period of twelve months. Successive
    releases have added participants: 306 in version 1.0, a further 136 in version 2.0 and a
    further 391 in version 3.0.0, reaching 833 adult participants.

data_collectors:
- role: researcher
  collector_details: >-
    Research teams, which may include medical, graduate or undergraduate students, coordinated
    with clinicians to identify eligible participants and conducted the collection sessions with a
    trained research assistant present.
- role: researcher
  collector_details: >-
    Clinicians and doctors, listed as co-investigators on the IRB protocol, provided the diagnoses
    and gold-standard validation. They were not directly compensated but were added to the
    consortium so that their names appear on consortium-level publications arising from the
    research.
- role: other
  collector_details: >-
    Hospital staff were not involved in scheduling but assisted in the logistics of coordinating
    data collection.

direct_collection:
- is_direct: true
  collection_details: >-
    Data were collected directly from the individuals in question, in clinic, with the assistance
    of a trained research assistant. Future collection is planned to occur remotely, but remote
    collection did not contribute to the initial releases.

sampling_strategies:
- is_sample: true
  is_random: false
  is_representative: false
  strategies: >-
    Non-probability sampling. Participants were recruited at high-volume expert clinics and
    community outreach clinics within participating academic institutions on the basis of a
    confirmed diagnosis in one of five disease cohorts, or as controls, against published
    inclusion and exclusion criteria; charts were screened for eligibility before the clinic day.
  source_data: >-
    Patients and healthy volunteers presenting at participating specialty clinics in the United
    States and Canada.
  why_not_representative: >-
    The data were collected at a limited number of geographic locations. The sample is skewed by
    disorder category, site and demographics, and groups with less trust in the medical system or
    in artificial intelligence, or living further from the collection sites, were less likely to be
    recruited. The consortium intends to improve representativeness by shifting to remote
    collection and designing recruitment to control for more variables.

raw_data_sources:
- source_description: >-
    Raw voice, speech, breathing and cough audio recordings captured by the Bridge2AI-Voice
    application, together with the questionnaire and clinical responses recorded alongside them.
  source_type: Prospectively collected audio recordings and questionnaire responses
  raw_data_format: >-
    WAV audio, converted to monaural and resampled to 16 kHz before feature extraction; REDCap and
    ReproSchema exports converted to tab-delimited phenotype tables.
  access_details: >-
    Raw audio is not included in the PhysioNet release. Access requires a completed Data Access
    Request Form and Data Use Agreement, review by the Data Access Compliance Office
    (DACO@b2ai-voice.org) and a signed Data Transfer and Use Agreement from an authorized
    institutional official; approved users receive the adult cohort audio through Synapse at
    https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/. The de-identified raw data are retained but are
    not publicly accessible.

preprocessing_strategies:
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Raw audio was converted to monaural and resampled to 16 kHz with a Butterworth anti-aliasing
    filter applied.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Spectrograms of dimension 201 by T were computed with a short-time fast Fourier transform
    using a 25 ms window, a 10 ms hop and a 400-point FFT, then downsampled by a factor of two in
    the time domain.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Mel spectrograms with 60 mel bins and 60 mel-frequency cepstral coefficients were computed
    with the same window, hop and FFT settings.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Articulatory features were produced with the Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc) package at
    50 Hz, giving electromagnetic articulography traces for six articulators (tongue dorsum,
    tongue body, tongue tip, lower incisor, upper lip and lower lip) together with loudness,
    periodicity and pitch estimates.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Phonetic posteriorgrams over 40 phoneme categories were generated at 100 Hz with the ppgs
    package.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Static acoustic, phonetic and prosodic features were extracted with openSMILE, Praat and
    parselmouth, and pitch contours with torchaudio, producing one row per recording in
    static_features.tsv.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    Raw audio files and questionnaire data retrieved from ReproSchema-UI or exported from REDCap
    were converted to a structure compliant with the Brain Imaging Data Structure v1.9.0, with
    phenotype tables grouped into confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaire
    and task folders.
- preprocessing_details: >-
    All processing was performed with the open-source b2aiprep library, which organizes and
    preprocesses the dataset, and senselab, which processes the audio files; version 3.1.0 was
    generated with b2aiprep v3.0.0.

cleaning_strategies:
- cleaning_details: >-
    No data cleaning was performed. An audit protocol was applied instead: missingness tables were
    generated, distributions and outliers checked, categorical responses checked against the
    schema, and quality control metrics run on the audio, including the amount of silence, the
    duration, and for speech tasks the agreement of the produced speech with the intended passage.
    From version 3.1.0 the resulting audio quality metrics are released alongside the features.

labeling_strategies:
- labeling_details: >-
    Diagnostic labels are the result of a clinical assessment of the participant. At each site a
    local clinician provided the diagnosis based on a clinical interview and appropriate work-up,
    using the gold-standard validation methods defined per cohort, such as laryngoscopy images and
    stroboscopy videos for voice disorders, CT and MRI of the brain for neurological disorders,
    and spirometry with flow-volume loops for airway conditions.
  annotations_per_item: 1
  data_annotation_protocol: Bridge2AI-Voice protocols and ICD-10 codes.
  annotator_demographics:
  - >-
    Typically the clinician at the site of data collection, or a clinician external to the study
    who had made a prior diagnostic assessment; a single labeler per instance.
- labeling_details: >-
    For the psychiatric disorders cohort the assessment was determined from the participant's
    electronic health record or from an active prescription, recorded outside the data collection
    session by an appropriately licensed clinician.

annotation_analyses:
- analysis_method: >-
    No inter-annotator agreement analysis was performed. A single labeler provided the diagnostic
    label for each instance, so no agreement statistic could be computed.
  annotation_quality_details: >-
    Labels are gold-standard clinical diagnoses provided by a clinician following the
    Bridge2AI-Voice protocols and ICD-10 codes. Human-level performance on the applications the
    dataset is intended to address is reported to vary widely. Certain machine-generated
    annotations, notably the Whisper transcriptions, were produced with off-the-shelf models that
    have not been audited for correctness.
  notes: >-
    The consortium recommends that any new labels or task definitions be described alongside the
    release of a model or publication, including the exact variables used for the determination.

machine_annotation_tools:
- tools:
  - OpenAI Whisper Large
  tool_descriptions: Used to generate transcriptions of the audio recordings.
  tool_accuracy:
  - >-
    Not audited. Certain aspects of the data, including transcription, were generated using
    off-the-shelf models that have not been audited for correctness.

variables:
- variable_name: participant_id
  data_type: identifier
  is_identifier: true
  notes: >-
    Unique identifier for the participant, present in every dense feature file and in the
    phenotype tables; it links feature records to phenotype rows.
- variable_name: session_id
  data_type: identifier
  is_identifier: true
  notes: >-
    Unique identifier for the recording session. A participant may have more than one session, so
    several sessions may share a participant_id.
- variable_name: task_name
  data_type: categorical
  notes: The acoustic task performed during the recording, drawn from the protocol's task inventory.
- variable_name: n_frames
  data_type: integer
  notes: >-
    The number of time frames associated with the feature stored in the record; feature tensors
    vary in length with the duration of the recording.
- variable_name: spectrogram
  data_type: array
  derivation: >-
    Short-time fast Fourier transform of the 16 kHz monaural waveform with a 25 ms window, a 10 ms
    hop and a 400-point FFT, downsampled by a factor of two in the time domain; dimension 201 by T.
  measurement_technique: torchaudio
  quality_notes: >-
    Absent for recordings that contain free speech, for sensitive records and for audio checks,
    and for recordings whose length or other properties prevented generation.
- variable_name: mel_spectrogram
  data_type: array
  derivation: >-
    Mel spectrogram with 60 mel bins computed with a 25 ms window, a 10 ms hop and a 400-point
    FFT; dimension 60 by T.
  measurement_technique: torchaudio
- variable_name: mfcc
  data_type: array
  derivation: >-
    Sixty mel-frequency cepstral coefficients computed from the mel spectrograms with the same
    window, hop and FFT parameters; dimension 60 by T.
  measurement_technique: torchaudio
- variable_name: pitch
  data_type: array
  derivation: >-
    Detected pitch (fundamental frequency) over time, of dimension T, with a minimum pitch of 80
    and a maximum of 500.
  measurement_technique: torchaudio
  minimum_value: 80.0
  maximum_value: 500.0
- variable_name: sparc_ema
  data_type: array
  derivation: >-
    Estimated electromagnetic articulography produced by a deep learning model at 50 Hz, of
    dimension T by 12, the twelve channels being the X and Y positions of six articulators: tongue
    dorsum, tongue body, tongue tip, lower incisor, upper lip and lower lip.
  measurement_technique: Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc)
- variable_name: sparc_loudness
  data_type: array
  derivation: >-
    Estimated loudness based on the average absolute amplitude of the audio waveform, of dimension
    T, computed with 20 ms windows.
  measurement_technique: Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc)
- variable_name: sparc_periodicity
  data_type: array
  derivation: >-
    Estimated periodicity, the confidence of pitch presence, derived from the audio with 20 ms
    windows, of dimension T.
  measurement_technique: Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc)
- variable_name: sparc_pitch
  data_type: array
  derivation: >-
    Estimated fundamental frequency of the audio signal computed with a different algorithm from
    the torchaudio pitch, over a range of 50 to 550 Hz, of dimension T.
  measurement_technique: Speech Articulatory Coding (sparc)
  unit: Hz
  minimum_value: 50.0
  maximum_value: 550.0
- variable_name: ppgs
  data_type: array
  derivation: >-
    Phonetic posteriorgram probabilities across 40 phoneme categories at a frame rate of 100 Hz,
    of dimension 40 by T.
  measurement_technique: ppgs package
  quality_notes: >-
    Removed for sensitive records and audio checks, and absent where the audio contained free
    speech.

distribution_formats:
- format: Apache Parquet
  notes: >-
    Dense per-recording feature tensors are distributed as Parquet files: ppgs.parquet,
    sparc_ema.parquet, sparc_loudness.parquet, sparc_periodicity.parquet, sparc_pitch.parquet,
    torchaudio_spectrogram.parquet, torchaudio_mfcc.parquet, torchaudio_pitch.parquet and
    torchaudio_mel_spectrogram.parquet, together with a per-recording metadata file.
- format: Tab-separated values
  notes: >-
    Static features (static_features.tsv), audio quality metrics (audio_quality_metrics.tsv) and
    the phenotype tables covering confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaires
    and tasks are distributed as TSV files.
- format: JSON
  notes: >-
    Every data file is accompanied by a JSON data dictionary with the same file stem, describing
    each column, the question asked of the participant where applicable, and the data type of the
    response.

    Version 1.0 was published on the Health Data Nexus at the end of November 2024; version 1.1 on

  regulatory_restrictions:
  - >-
    No export controls or other regulatory restrictions apply to the dataset or to individual

  hipaa_compliant: compliant
  confidentiality_level: restricted
  other_compliance: >-
    The data are covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality, which must be asserted against

    partners, which hold pre-negotiated agreements with the NIH for data privacy and HIPAA
